Le Monde (English edition), by Thibaud Metais and Bastien Scordia — "French civil servants take to the streets ahead of key budget meeting". Published 30 September 2026, 11:06 Paris time (10:06 BST). CONFIRMED 30 Sep publication; EVENT was Tuesday 29 September 2026.
Retrieved via Exa search snippet (the article's own words).

STANDFIRST (verbatim): "Street turnout exceeded that of the previous major public sector demonstration, in December 2024, though strike rates were lower, leaving unions weighing their next move ahead of Friday's meeting with the government."

BODY (verbatim as returned):
"Public servants' unions could hardly have chosen a more symbolic spot to launch their protest. On Tuesday, September 29, one of the two Paris marches of civil servants, called to denounce the erosion of public employees' purchasing power among other grievances, set off from outside a branch of Picard, the popular frozen food chain, a stone's throw from Place de la Republique. The symbolism was hard to miss after Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's government announced another public sector pay freeze for 2027, though union members insisted it was pure coincidence. The second march, made up of firefighters, set off from Place d'Italie before heading, like the first, to Place de la Nation.

With nearly 170 rallies organized across France, the union coalition had threatened a 'black day' of disruption and hoped for a turnout comparable to that of December 5, 2024, the last major day of protest in the public sector. Their gamble partly paid off, at least in terms of how many protesters turned up for the marches. According to the CGT, one of the country's main worker's unions, more than 300,000 people marched nationwide, including 70,000 in Paris. The interior ministry put the national figure at 206,000, with 30,000 in the capital, among them 8,000 firefighters. Both estimates were higher than those recorded at the 2024 marches."

KEY EXTRA SPECIFICS THIS GIVES OVER AL JAZEERA:
- Prime Minister named: Sebastien Lecornu.
- Interior ministry national figure: 206,000 (vs CGT's 300,000+).
- CGT Paris figure 70,000 vs interior ministry 30,000; 8,000 firefighters in Paris.
- Nearly 170 rallies nationwide; unions' "black day" framing.
- Both turnout estimates exceeded the 5 December 2024 public-sector marches.
- A further union meeting with the government is set for FRIDAY.
